Aṇīcin Mauna.--He is mentioned as an authority on ritual, and contemporary with jābāla and citra gauśrāyaṇi or gauśra, in the kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes xxiii. 5.

Āṇi.--This word, which is found in the Rigveda, but rarely later, appears to be best taken with Roth and Zimmer as denoting the part of the axle of the chariot which is inserted into the nave of the wheel. Sāyaṇa renders it as lynch-pin, and this sense is accepted by Leumann, being apparently also found in the nirukta. In one place in the Rigveda the word appears by synecdoche to denote the whole chariot, but the passage is, according to Geldner, completely obscure.
Foot notes i. 35, 6; v. 43, 8.
